newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinian official criticises U.S. Mideast policy.
newsitem.headline: Palestinian official criticises U.S. Mideast policy.

text.p: A senior Palestinian official said on Saturday the United States should be "more neutral" in its Middle East policy and called on Washington to upgrade the level of its involvement in efforts to salvage the peace process.

"The current crisis in the PLO-Israeli peace process requires the involvement of U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright if the U.S. intends to find solutions," said Tayeb Abdel-Rahim, general secretary of the Palestinian presidency.

In an indirect criticism of U.S. special envoy Dennis Ross, Abdel-Rahim said: "I am not doubting anyone, but I am saying that the U.S. administration should be more neutral and must adhere more to the basis of the peace process."
Peace negotiations between the Palestinians and Israelis have been suspended since Israel's groundbreaking on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.

The U.S. sent Ross to the region earlier this month for talks with the Palestinian Authority and Israel to find ways to bring the sides back to the negotiating table. Afterwards the United States said major gaps remained between the two sides.
Ross is the main contact between the Palestinian Authority and the U.S. administration.
Marwan Kanafani, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's spokesman, said Ross would be returning to the region on May 2.
Palestinian officials complained that during Ross's talks with PLO leaders, he was not "even-handed" and was trying to persuade them to accept Israel's position.

Palestinians were angered by the United States, the main broker in the Arab-Israeli peace process, for vetoing two U.N. Security Council resolutions criticising Israel over settlement building in Arab East Jerusalem.
On Friday, the U.S. again voted against a U.N. General Assembly resolution calling for an immediate halt to the settlement's construction.

"During President Arafat's visit to Washington and during the visit of the senior Palestinian delegation to Washington this month, we were surprised to learn that a lot of information was not conveyed to the U.S. administration at higher levels," Abdel-Rahim said.
He recalled a telephone conversation between Albright and Arafat after a bombing by a Moslem militant in a Tel Aviv cafe killed three Israeli women on March 21.

"Secretary Albright talked to Arafat about terrorism and the need to restore security cooperation with Israel, but Arafat asked her why they didn't call him to give him condolences for the killing of five Palestinians by Israeli soldiers in Hebron," he said.
"She said she wasn't informed about it and promised to call back. She called after two hours and said she was conveying President Clinton's condolences to him," he added.
"This and many other incidents show us that only selected information is conveyed to officials at higher levels at the State Department," Abdel-Rahim said.
